newsitem.title: USA: NJ voters think they pay more taxes, poll.
newsitem.headline: NJ voters think they pay more taxes, poll.

text.p: Most New Jersey voters think they pay more taxes even though Republican Governor Christine Todd Whitman has followed through on her promise to cut income tax, according to an opinion poll released Thursday.
The Quinnipiac College Poll also found that 67 percent of those polled are "very satisfied" or "somewhat satisfied" with the ways things are going in the state.
Whitman, one of the nation's best known Republican governors, was frequently suggested as a possible running mate to former Sen. Robert Dole in his failed bid for the White House last year.
She comes up for re-election in November with polls showing she should win handily against any of her potential Democratic opponents.

The pollsters at the Hamden, Connecticut, college said although there had been a series of tax decreases and increases across the state, 61 percent of voters polled said they pay more state and local taxes than they did three years ago.
"That's not a plus for the Governor -- particularly a governor who promised to cut state income taxes and then did," said Maurice Carroll, director of the Quinnipiac College Polling Institute.

"Her critics have countered that the state tax cut forced local governments to raise property taxes. No matter what the Governor or her opponents have said or done, voters believe that their taxes have gone up."
Quinnipiac College surveyed 875 New Jersey residents who said they were registered voters. The poll was conducted Feb. 11-16 and has a margin of error of plus or minus 3.3 percent.
It found that most voters want New Jersey politicians to give priority to improving education, reducing crime and car insurance rates and lowering unemployment.
